name: Wayne Rodrigues & Danielle Brisebois
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 pop-2000s — Wayne Rodrigues & Danielle Brisebois
notes: The Venice Beach pair behind mid-2000s modal uplift pop: 100–115 straight, backbeat on 2&4. The harmonic signature is stated as the defining fact of their productions and is **modal rather than functional** — F Mixolydian, "looping I–♭VII–IV with **no dominant chord anywhere**" — so mixolydian outweighs major in the scales, the I–bVII–IV loop dominates, and no authored family contains a V. Three drum deltas are quoted: "kick 1 and the '&' of 3", "16th hat with an open hat **before** the backbeat" (the open hat on "1&" and "3&"), and "tambourine from chorus 1"; the fourth stated fact, "a total drum drop-out before the last chorus", is `dropOutBeats` at 0.95. What separates this model from the artist entry that shares the flagship is the low end and the palette: "rounded synth bass on roots with an 8th pulse, **reinforced by a B3 organ pedal in the low mid**", which is `boom_chick` at 0.94 with the register reaching lower than a plain pop bass, plus **turntables** in the perc block. The gospel choir "answering the lead in block harmony" is the sustained-pad counter at a real ratio, and the lead is "syllable-dense and near-spoken in the verse and wide and sustained in the chorus". ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research rates it high-medium and marks the tempo **[LOW-CONF]**; `bpm.mode` 106 is this author's centre of the stated band. ⚠ Every drum probability here is **INFERRED**. ⚠ **`bassline.rhythm` is `boom_chick`, not `reese_sustain`** — the research names the figure outright: *“rounded synth bass on roots with an 8th pulse, reinforced by a B3 organ pedal in the low mid”*. A held `reese_sustain` writes one note per chord and says the opposite of what the entry describes.
